note: Batch 07: the 28 downloaded-but-uncarded SharePoint files (government, HySecure, HyID, HyWorks, pharma, VDI/TCO). Written from corpus/text/*.txt, every file read in full. Three findings shape these cards. (1) The HySecure 'Product-v2', '- Small' and '- Big' PDFs are NOT size variants: the base file is a full-portfolio 'Work from Anywhere' deck (HySecure, HyID, HyWorks, HyLabs, Nano, HyDesk), Small is a HySecure-only edition, and Big is Small plus the Gartner delivery-model slides, a company/customer appendix and web-proxy explanations - Big is the canonical HySecure edition. (2) Several documents carry the only Fortinet / Palo Alto / WireGuard / OpenVPN comparisons in the library (HySecure Product-v2 decks, Gateway as a Service, VDI vs VPN), which the 25 Sep content-gap test reported as missing - they are 2021-2024 and internal, but they exist. (3) The 2025-26 government decks reuse each other's slides heavily and contain internal contradictions (DSCI award 2024 vs 2025, 900+ vs 850+ customers, 90,000 vs 60,000 MFA users for the same bank, 'ISO 270001'); stale_risk names them so a rep does not quote the wrong one. Real customer names appear only in client_actual; brief, outcomes and use_for use descriptors.

cards.title: Accops HySecure ZTNA Gateway: Product Deck (Extended Edition, 2021)
cards.client: Call-centre and BYOD work-from-home deployments; appendix lists Japanese, Middle East and European government, healthcare and manufacturing customers
cards.client_actual: Kyoto University, Ibaraki Prefectural, Dubai Courts, City Pharmacy LLC, Zulekha Hospital, Al Zahra Hospital, Ahalia Medical Group, Fresenius Kabi, Kalle GmbH (customer logo list)
cards.key_problem: A layer-3 VPN bridges an unmanaged home PC into the corporate network, exposes data-centre subnets to any malware on it, and gives IT no control over data copy, internet use or which device the user logs in from.
key_outcomes: Three tunnel types in one gateway: L7 reverse proxy (clientless), L4 SPAN app tunnels (TLS 1.2), L3 Turbo tunnel (Noise protocol, ChaCha20-Poly1305) for VoIP
Turbo benchmark: 1,011 Mbps vs 825-881 Mbps for IPsec and 258 Mbps for OpenVPN; 8.9 vs 7.55 Mbps and 459 vs 244 KB/s download against a Palo Alto hardware appliance while running on a VM
Sizing per 8 vCPU VM: ~2,500-5,000 users (L7), ~2,000-3,000 (L4, 16 GB RAM), 2,000-5,000 CCU per node for Cisco / Palo Alto / Fortinet
Device binding by OS, CPU, HDD, motherboard and MAC IDs; host scan for AV, firewall, Windows updates; geo-location and impossible-travel reports
Four WFH architecture models for call-centre agents (gateway only, gateway + VDI, gateway + Nano bootable USB, all three) with pros, cons and a 14-control security comparison
Security of the appliance: CIS-hardened Linux, TLS 1.2/1.3, Qualys SSL A+, VAPT by a CERT-In empanelled lab, 12+ node HA clusters
Editions: Gold, Silver, Platinum; perpetual or subscription, concurrent or named users
cards.brief: The fullest of the three 2021 HySecure 'Product-v2' PDFs and the one to treat as canonical. It explains the gateway's three access modes (clientless L7, L4 SPAN app tunnels, L3 Turbo), why per-application tunnels hide the data centre where a layer-3 VPN exposes it, and the endpoint controls a VPN lacks: internet whitelisting without a web proxy, clipboard / print-screen / screen-share blocking, watermarking, device binding and host scan. It includes Turbo throughput and latency benchmarks against IPsec, OpenVPN and a Palo Alto appliance; Gartner-sourced delivery-model and BYOPC risk matrices; four call-centre WFH architectures with and without VDI and the Nano secure USB; how HySecure co-exists with an existing VPN and with cloud web proxies (including the SSH-bypass loophole in web-proxy agents); a three-table comparison of Accops L7/L4/L3 against WireGuard, OpenVPN and Cisco / Palo Alto / Fortinet covering deployment, security, cost and per-VM sizing; and a feature grid against Microsoft WVD, Citrix/VMware, Zscaler/McAfee, F5/Palo Alto and Okta/Cisco Duo. An appendix carries the 2021 company profile and customer logo list.
cards.use_for: A presales or architecture conversation about replacing a Cisco, Palo Alto or Fortinet VPN, sizing a HySecure gateway, VoIP / call-centre remote access, or explaining how ZTNA co-exists with an existing VPN or cloud web proxy. The closest thing the library has to a Fortinet comparison.
cards.stale_risk: Copyright 2021 on every slide. Company figures (600+ customers, 600,000+ users, 150+ team) are well below current material (900+ customers, 2M+ users). Competitor claims (Cisco Duo licensing, 'Zscaler SaaS only', 'Microsoft WVD') are 2021 positions - WVD is now Azure Virtual Desktop. Turbo sizing row reads '~5000-1000 users per VM', an obvious typo. For current product specs use the HySecure Datasheet V5 2026 (public).
cards.internal_reason: Marked 'Accops Confidential' on every slide; contains named competitor benchmarks and a customer logo list.
cards.needs_human: Near-duplicate family: 'Accops - HySecure - Product-v2.pdf' (Jul 2021, a different full-portfolio deck), '- Small.pdf' (Nov 2021, a subset of this one) and this '- Big.pdf' (Apr 2022 in SharePoint). Big contains everything in Small plus the Gartner matrices, company appendix and web-proxy notes, so Big is canonical and Small can be retired. Confirm, and confirm whether the .pptx twins in the same folder are the same editions.

Five editions: HyWorks VDI, Essentials, Advanced, Enterprise, Platinum, with a feature matrix; named, device or concurrent licensing
Cases: 270-user thin-client VDI in remote factories; 700-user VDI for SAP at a pharma company; vendor cheque-collection access for a global bank
CRM over 96 kbps branch links with ~100x faster access (10 minutes to 10 seconds) via virtual browser; core-banking app delivery to SaaS customers; SWIFT isolation
cards.brief: An early HyWorks introduction deck. It sets out the pain of desktop computing, the virtualisation methods (application virtualisation, shared hosted desktops, hosted virtual desktops) with a comparison of shared vs hosted desktops, HyWorks functions and deployment diagram, a detailed 'HyWorks vs direct RDP' table, a competitive landscape against Citrix, VMware, Ericom, Parallels and Workspot, add-ons, licensing, the five editions with a feature matrix, platform support, and a long run of banking and enterprise use cases: factory thin clients, SAP delivery at a pharma company, vendor access for a global bank, CRM over low-bandwidth branches, core-banking delivery, helpdesk without internet, privileged access audit, developer sandboxes and SWIFT isolation.

cards.stale_risk: Copyright 2017. Thin clients cut TCO by as much as 40% compared with conventional desktops

cards.title: AccOps VDI: A Complete Solution to Replace Thick-PC Computing (2-Pager, 2021)
cards.client: A defence research lab, a nuclear research campus and a large private bank
cards.client_actual: DRDO Delhi, IGCAR Kalpakkam, Axis Bank
cards.key_problem: Thick PCs need replacing every 4-5 years, constant patching and per-PC security licences, leak data, and make onboarding users and vendors slow.
key_outcomes: Thin/zero clients last 7-10 years and use one-tenth of a PC's electricity
Endpoint security licensing drops to 1/40th of PC-based computing
Data never leaves the data centre; apps not visible on the network
Case: a defence lab separated internet from the local network via a virtual browser and blocked USB and data copy
Case: a nuclear research campus with 1,000+ scientists isolated internet and adopted thin clients
Case: 26,000 corporate and back-office staff of a private bank working from home on Accops VDI
cards.brief: A two-page VDI explainer and TCO argument. It lists the problems of PC-based computing, explains how Accops VDI hosts applications and desktops on data-centre VMs (sized to the user base and apps such as MS Office, SAP and Tally) accessed from existing PCs, thin clients or zero clients, and quantifies the benefits: 7-10 year thin-client life at one-tenth the power, security licences at 1/40th, no data on endpoints, any-device access and faster onboarding. Three short cases cover a defence lab, a nuclear research campus and a large private bank's 26,000-user work-from-home rollout.
cards.use_for: An early VDI or thin-client conversation where the buyer wants the cost and security argument in two pages. Check figures before sending.
cards.stale_risk: Copyright 2020-2021, old 'AccOps' branding and '500+ customers & 600,000+ users'. For a current, detailed VDI cost case use the 2025 'VDI for Govt - TCO' deck.

cards.key_problem: Hybrid work is permanent, but on-premise VDI takes weeks or months to deploy, needs scarce skills and capex, and still has to meet security and compliance requirements across unmanaged devices.

Accounting firm: attrition down 70% and office rent down ~50% after enabling remote work
IT services provider: opex down 25%
Third-largest public sector bank: SWIFT and CBS from a single PC, biometric auth and DLP, 50% lower TCO than competitor solutions
Covers VDI for contact centres with VoIP, graphics-rich apps, device approval, and contextual access for RBI and GLBA compliance
Cites Gartner: 60% of employees prefer hybrid; 76% saw culture improve after remote work
cards.brief: A 2023 press-ready whitepaper introducing Accops Managed Desktops, Accops' turnkey subscription Desktop-as-a-Service. It frames the hybrid-work challenge (cyber risk, diverse devices, compliance, uninterrupted access), then describes AMD as a single platform combining virtualisation, ZTNA and IAM with desktop profiles, contextual access, DLP, MFA, capacity planning, thin-client management and experience monitoring. cards.title: What Does Your Remote Workforce Need - VPN or VDI? (Guidance Whitepaper, Nov 2021)
cards.key_problem: Organisations choosing a remote-work solution treat VPN and VDI as alternatives, but a VPN only provides connectivity and bridges a possibly infected device into the corporate network.
key_outcomes: Eight-point comparison: security, on-demand app delivery, DLP, low-bandwidth access, emergency access from alternate devices, data backup, non-Windows devices, auditing and monitoring
With VDI plus L4-L7 ZTNA only screen bitmaps and input travel; corporate IPs are never exposed
New apps provisioned in minutes instead of days; any device with a browser works
Bandwidth stays constant regardless of application weight
VDI gives per-application, per-user audit and productivity monitoring that VPNs cannot
cards.brief: A vendor-light guidance paper, last updated 9 November 2021, arguing that comparing VPN with VDI is a category error: a VPN is a connectivity tool, Accops VDI is a complete workspace with Zero Trust access, access management and DLP. It works through eight business needs - security while remote, on-demand application delivery, data-leakage prevention, performance over home bandwidth, emergency access when a PC fails, central backup, non-Windows devices, and auditing and monitoring - explaining in each why VPNs fall short and VDI with ZTNA does not.
cards.use_for: A CIO or IT head asking 'why not just give everyone a VPN?' or evaluating VPN vs VDI for a sustained remote workforce. Plain enough to send early in a cycle.
cards.stale_risk: Dated November 2021 and argues from the Covid-era shift; the reasoning holds but the framing is dated.
cards.internal_reason: No public URL confirmed. Generic guidance with no customer detail - a candidate for publication.
